name: api-stability-tier
_stage_vocabulary_open_question: UNRESOLVED, and it must be resolved BEFORE any unknown_stage row for this lane is frozen. Measured: this lane observes 750 artifacts and reports 750 unknown_stage — a 100% failure rate on one code, which indicates a VOCABULARY MISMATCH rather than 750 individually-wrong artifacts. All 750 registry/catalog/*.yaml declare `api_stability: preview`, and `preview` is canonical, not a placeholder: docs/machine-readable/contracts.json `_metadata.stability_tiers` is [preview, stable, GA], intelligence/core/catalog-domain `enum ApiStability` is {Preview, Stable, Ga}, and marketplace/facade/dev-cli/src/governance_gates.rs validate_claim_ceiling_gate enforces FoundationClaimCeiling::preview_foundation() = max Preview over this exact directory. So the `stages` list below ({experimental, stable, deprecated, removed}) is a DIFFERENT vocabulary that shares only `stable` — the config is mismatched to its corpus, the corpus is not in debt. Freezing 750 unknown_stage would certify that mismatch as corpus debt and make it permanent, and the debt would be UNRETIRABLE: raising any crate above preview is exactly what the claim-ceiling gate rejects. Aligning this vocabulary to [preview, stable, GA] instead yields a lane that enforces canonical-tier conformance across 750 files born-blocking (any future non-canonical value is an unbaselined_violation immediately) and still reds via lane_discovered_nothing if the root moves away. Note `defaults.case_insensitive_stage_match` is true, so GA/ga need not be spelled twice. The vocabulary decision is deliberately NOT taken in this commit.
purpose: Lifecycle state machine for API stability tier transitions from experimental through removal.
